Remove copies of one service published in two files

Source: R/gtfs_deduplicate_copies.R
gtfs_deduplicate_copies.Rd

[gtfs_deduplicate()] recognises a journey only when two trips carry it with identical times at every stop, under one operator name. That misses a whole class of duplicates in merged TransXChange feeds: one timetable written out twice by two publishers. Each publisher interpolates the times at the stops between timing points its own way, and files the operator under its own name, so no two copies agree call by call even though every journey leaves the same first stop at the same minute.

This function compares *services* instead of trips. Where two services of the same line and mode, from different source files, start most of their journeys at the same stop at the same time, one is a copy of the other: the lower ranked one loses its journeys on every date the higher ranked one also runs them.

Usage

gtfs_deduplicate_copies(
  gtfs,
  min_share = 0.8,
  min_shared = 2L,
  match = c("start", "ends"),
  keep = c("newer", "longer", "more_trips"),
  scope = c("trips", "route"),
  fixed_track = c(0L, 1L, 2L),
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

gtfs

a gtfs object

min_share

numeric between 0 and 1, the share of one service's distinct journey starts (first stop and departure time) that must also be starts of the other before the two are called copies. Default 0.8.

min_shared

integer, the fewest shared starts that can make two services copies. Default 2, so that one coincident journey never condemns a service.

match

`"start"` (the default) matches journeys on their first stop and departure time; `"ends"` also requires the same last stop and arrival time, which is stricter and misses a copy that was re-routed or re-timed towards its end.

keep

character, the order in which the criteria decide which copy is kept, best first. `"newer"` prefers the service whose calendar starts later - the more recently published version - and only discriminates on a feed whose calendars have not been trimmed to a common window; `"longer"` prefers the service whose journeys call at more stops (finer detail, or a whole route rather than one region's share of it); `"more_trips"` prefers the service with more journeys. Remaining ties go to the lower `route_id`.

scope

`"trips"` (the default) removes only the lower ranked copy's journeys that match a journey of the kept copy, on the dates both run. `"route"` also removes its unmatched journeys on dates the kept copy runs, treating it as a superseded version of the whole timetable. Even then a service is only removed wholesale if its own share of matched starts reaches `min_share`; a larger service that merely contains a smaller one loses only the matched journeys.

fixed_track

integer vector of `route_type`s left out. Duplicates on rail, metro and tram are already handled by [gtfs_deduplicate()]'s termini test. Default `c(0, 1, 2)`.

quiet

logical, suppress the summary message

Value

the gtfs object with the copies' journeys removed or their dates trimmed. A data.frame describing every pair of copies found, and what was done about it, is attached as attribute `"copies_report"`.

Details

**Which routes are one service.** A route is identified with its source service: the `[ServiceCode: ...]` that [transxchange2gtfs()] writes into `route_desc`, together with `agency_id`. Routes of one service are variants of one file and are never compared with each other - that is [gtfs_deduplicate()]'s job. A feed without ServiceCodes falls back to `route_id`.

**When two services are copies.** They must share `route_short_name` and `route_type`, and at least `min_share` of the distinct journey starts of one of them (and at least `min_shared` starts) must be starts of the other. The operator is deliberately not compared: in the cases this exists for, the two copies name the operator differently ("Arriva" against "Arriva Midlands", both NOC AMID) or not at all the same operator (Go-Ahead's superseded export of London route 439 against Transport for London's current file naming Metrobus).

A line number alone could not make two services copies: two towns' route 1 do not leave the same stop. Two operators running a joint timetable do not either, because they share the departures out rather than repeat them.

**What is removed.** Dates are respected throughout. A journey of the copy is removed on the dates the kept service runs a journey with the same start (scope `"trips"`) or runs at all (scope `"route"`). If that is every date the journey runs, the trip is deleted; if it is some of them, the trip is moved to a new service that no longer runs on those dates; if none, it is left alone. A superseded open-ended file therefore loses its journeys only from the date its successor begins.

Groups of three or more copies are ranked together, and each loses its journeys to every higher ranked service it is a copy of.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
gtfs <- gtfs_merge(list(gtfs_a, gtfs_b), force = TRUE)
gtfs <- gtfs_deduplicate_copies(gtfs)
attr(gtfs, "copies_report")
} # }
